## Cold open

> SCENE (states): Bremen lights up on the map of Germany.
> Bremen | Stadtstaat

[dramatic] [[Bremen]] is the smallest German state, and it's made up of two cities: Bremen and Bremerhaven, about sixty kilometres apart on the river Weser. Its official name is the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen.

[dramatic] If you take the citizenship test in Bremen, three of your thirty-three questions are about the state you live in. They come from a list of just ten. Here are all ten, with the answers.

> SCENE (title): Title card.
> BREMEN

## On the map

{Q348}

> SCENE (question): Question card #348. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] The exam shows a map with four states, numbered. [[Welches Bundesland ist Bremen?]] Which federal state is Bremen?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[1]]. Number one: the small city-state in the north-west, surrounded by Lower Saxony.


{Q347}

> SCENE (question): Question card #347. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] [[Was ist ein deutscher Stadtstaat?]] Which of these is a German city-state?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[Bremen]]. There are three city-states: Berlin, Hamburg and Bremen. Each one is a city and a state at the same time.


## Flag and coat of arms

{Q345}

> SCENE (question): Question card #345. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] [[Welche Farben hat die Landesflagge von Bremen?]] What are the colors of the state flag of Bremen?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[rot-weiß]]. Red and white, in stripes and checks.


{Q341}

> SCENE (question): Question card #341. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] The exam shows four coats of arms. [[Welches Wappen gehört zur Freien Hansestadt Bremen?]] Which coat of arms belongs to the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[Bild 3]], picture three: a silver key on a red shield.


## How it's run

{Q342}

> SCENE (question): Question card #342. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] [[Welches ist ein Stadtteil von Bremen?]] Which of these is a district of Bremen?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[Hemelingen]]. The others are elsewhere: [[Altona]] is in [[Hamburg]], [[Pankow]] is in [[Berlin]], and [[Babelsberg]] is in [[Brandenburg]].


{Q343}

> SCENE (question): Question card #343. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] [[Für wie viele Jahre wird das Landesparlament in Bremen gewählt?]] For how many years is the state parliament in Bremen elected?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[4]]. Four years. Bremen is the only state that still elects its parliament for four years; all the others have moved to five.


{Q344}

> SCENE (question): Question card #344. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] [[Ab welchem Alter darf man in Bremen bei den Wahlen zur Bürgerschaft (Landtag) wählen?]] At what age are you allowed to vote in the elections for the Bürgerschaft (state parliament) in Bremen?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[16]]. Here, you can vote for the state parliament from sixteen. It differs from state to state. For the Bundestag, it's eighteen everywhere.


{Q349}

> SCENE (question): Question card #349. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.
> @ Präsidentin oder Präsident des Senates

[dramatic] [[Wie nennt man die Regierungschefin oder den Regierungschef des Stadtstaates Bremen?]] What is the title of the head of government of the city-state of Bremen?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[Präsidentin oder Präsident des Senates]], the president of the senate. In Bremen, the senate is the state government, and its president is also the city's mayor. Don't mix it up with Berlin's governing mayor, or Hamburg's first mayor.


{Q350}

> SCENE (question): Question card #350. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.
> @ Senatorin oder Senator für Außenbeziehungen

[dramatic] And a question with a [[nicht]]. [[Welche Senatorin oder welchen Senator hat Bremen nicht?]] Which senator does Bremen not have?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[Senatorin oder Senator für Außenbeziehungen]], a senator for foreign relations. In a city-state, the ministers are called senators. Finance, justice and the interior: Bremen has all of those. Foreign policy is the federation's job.


{Q346}

> SCENE (question): Question card #346. Three seconds to guess, then the answer highlights.

[dramatic] [[Wo können Sie sich in Bremen über politische Themen informieren?]] Where can you find information on political topics in Bremen?

[countdown] [dramatic] [[bei der Landeszentrale für politische Bildung]], the state centre for civic education. Every state has one. It's free, it belongs to no party, and it has material on politics in plain language.


## What to remember for the exam

> SCENE (words): The words appear one by one, then settle into a grid.
> Hemelingen, rot-weiß, Präsident des Senates

[dramatic] Three answers to hold on to: [[Hemelingen]]. [[rot-weiß]]. And [[Präsident des Senates]].
